Former Prayer Hall in the Oppenheimer-Stift in Hamburg

Former Synagogue · Hamburg, Germany

The Oppenheimer-Stift at Kielortallee 22–24 was a residential foundation for Orthodox Jewish community members and included a synagogue. The new complex first came into use in 1909. Its prayer hall served the residents until 1938, when Jewish religious life was suppressed under National Socialism. Worship resumed there after the Second World War in 1945, but the prayer hall closed in 1960. The surviving building complex no longer functions as a synagogue. This record is retained as the mapped entry for the former Oppenheimer-Stift prayer hall.
